Ms. Promise La'Shae Hampton was born to Letriace Hampton and Tony Bennett on October 20, 2000 in Jackson, MS. She was a student at Powell Middle School in Jackson, MS. Promise went to be with the Lord on Friday, August 12, 2016 at University of MS Medical Center here in Jackson, MS surrounded by family and friends. She was a happy and entergetic child, she had many friends who loved being with her, she liked dancing, singing, taking pictures, and being outdoors. She became an avid fisher, compliments of her loving grandpa.

webpage.text:
Children tell of surviving fatal hit and run, family grieves

Brandon Jones' little brother and his girlfriend were run down in front of his eyes by a vehicle he'd noticed driving past them multiple times as they walked home from a gas station down Jackson's Northside Drive Friday night.

The five of them — Brandon, 15; his little brother, Bryan Jones, 13; Brandon's girlfriend, Promise Hampton, 15; his little sister, Trinity Gray, 11; and their godsister, Valencia Bass, 11, were coming back from getting drinks for Trinity's sleepover birthday party around 11:30 p.m. The family had just moved into a new house on Hanging Moss Road a week earlier, and the gas station was only a few hundred yards away.

The five young people had noticed a blue Jeep Cherokee that had passed them a few times. Valencia had even pointed out that maybe they should go home because the Jeep seemed to be "circling."

"He kept going past, and I’m like, 'Why does this truck just keep on passing?' Promise was talking to me and my brother was on the right side of me, and I saw him in the corner of my eye just passing by, passing by," Brandon said.

Valencia and Trinity were a little way ahead of the others on the sidewalk when Brandon stopped to tie up his pants.

"I heard tires screeching and I saw that Jeep coming really fast, and I told them, 'Watch out, watch out,' and my sisters moved out of the way," Brandon said, his eyes haunted. "As soon as they looked back they got hit before they could get out of the way."

"He drove over the sidewalk to run them over," Valencia said.

"My mind went blank, I was just screaming and crying," Brandon said. "I was very hurt when that happened, and the sound that it did, it sounded like a car crash."

The children's father, Aaron Haynes, had gone to bed, but his wife Shirlene and her friend were still awake. The silence woke him up.

"I knew the kids weren’t in the house, because normally you can hear them playing around and it was so quiet, so I asked my wife, 'Where are the kids?'" he said. "That’s when my oldest son Brandon came in the house. It was like I was dreaming. He came in the room and I guess because he panicked, he showed us, 'I’ve got blood on my hand, we’ve got to hurry up, Bryan and Promise just got hit.'

"And when I got there, my son was just laying there, just left there like he was a piece of trash or something," Aaron Haynes said, breaking down.

Culpable negligent homicide charges filed

William Gilbert, 50, turned himself in on Saturday, several hours after the incident. He was given a $25,000 bond Monday for felony leaving the scene of an accident. On Tuesday, after investigators developed more information, Gilbert was also charged with two counts of culpable negligent homicide.

Bryan's family said they were told Gilbert lived in Promise's apartment complex, but none of them knew him. It doesn't appear that Promise knew him either.

"She would always tell me everything that goes on, but she never told me about no stalker problems or anything like that," Brandon said.

The two teens, who were taken to the University of Mississippi Medical Center Friday night, both died the next day. Hinds County Coroner Sharon Grisham-Stewart said the teens died from blunt force trauma. Their bodies have been sent to the state crime lab for autopsy to obtain documentation of their exact injuries, officials said.

The vehicle was found on Belmede Place with heavy damage to the front end, Jackson Police Department officials said. Evidence from the scene matched the vehicle.

Police aren't commenting on toxicology tests or other questions surrounding why Gilbert's vehicle allegedly left the road and ended up on the sidewalk Friday night.

'He wanted to be an architect and a police officer'

Bryan Jones was a little force of nature.

"He wanted to be an architect and a police officer, he wanted to build things, and he would help me build things," Brandon said. "When I’m crying or something, he’d make me laugh and feel better. He was an awesome brother, he was there for me and he was awesome. And that was my only brother... it’s hard losing him because he’s my only brother."

He loved to cook. He was a master with the Legos. He did well in school. He greeted his parents every day with a good morning kiss.

"When you see Bryan, you heard Bryan," Shirlene said. "He was playing with his Legos or listening to music, playing games, and now it’s not the same."

He was instrumental in decorating the family living room, Shirlene Haynes said, and his decoration style focused on art featuring how important family and faith was. A framed picture on the wall behind them read, "Our family is a circle of strength and love."

"I’m still blessed, and I know God is in control, I thank God for sparing the other children," Shirlene said.

Bryan constantly kept tabs on where his family was, they said.

"He was very caring. Every day he’d wake up and come to our room and hug us and kiss us good morning. Throughout the day, he was the type of kid that would come to us, 'Are you OK, everything OK?'" Shirlene said. "He would check on us and tell us he loved us, I’m so serious, every 15-30 minutes. Then he'd say, 'OK  I love you,' then he’d go back to playing outside or playing with his Legos."

"When I was on my phone in my room  he’d run and jump on my bed and we’d play fight," Trinity said, and when Aaron laughed at that memory, it might have been the only time he had smiled all day.

'He killed my brother and my girlfriend'

Brandon held his composure. He answered questions matter-of-factly, but just below the surface of his calm demeanor is a deep sadness.

"What all three of us have seen, it will never leave our minds, and it was really hard. It was my first time seeing anyone..." he trailed off.

A moment later, he added to the thought in a way that simple words don't do justice.

"He didn’t just kill two teens. He killed my brother and Promise. He didn’t just kill two teens. He killed my brother and my girlfriend," he said.

Brandon and Promise had been together for more than two years, he said.

"We didn’t have many breakups and she was really cool. Before she passed, she had bought me something," he said. "I was really happy. No girl had ever bought me something, she was the first one, and I loved her so much."

Promise was generous like that. She was kind to her boyfriend's little sister, and that wasn't lost on Trinity.

"She brought me some stuff for my birthday, some bracelets and some soap and some nail polishes," she said. "I was really happy."

Aaron and Shirlene loved Promise too, and at least once during the interview, Shirlene referred to her as her own.

"Promise, she was an awesome kid," she said. "(William Gilbert) took so much away from us."

'You crushed every bone in his body and left him there'

Aaron and Shirlene know they've got a healing process ahead. Persevering through the snail's pace of the legal process is the least of it. And both have words for William Gilbert, the man accused of killing their son.

"I just, if I could say anything, I’d want to know why you took my son’s life, why you just hit him and left him, you didn’t even stop to see if he was OK," Aaron said. "You hit my son and you ran him completely over and crushed every bone in his body and left him there like a piece of trash. Why?"

"Not only our son. Promise, she didn’t deserve it, and Bryan, too. You made it worse when you left the scene, and you kept going. And you tried to hit my other two children," Shirlene said. "Why did you do it? It’s going to take some time to forgive him, and I ask God to give me strength. I’m a child of God and I know I have to forgive."

The family has started a GoFundMe account to try to raise money for funeral expenses. No one expects to bury their child.

Both of them wish they could say one more thing to Bryan, too.

"I’d say baby, you know how much I love you, I’ll always love you and not a day will go by that I won’t think about you," Shirlene said.

"I’d just tell him how much I love him and care for him, I'd do anything for him," said Aaron.

If you know anything about Gilbert's activities on Friday night, please call Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1234.

webpage.text:
Suspect in deadly hit and run denied bond

JACKSON, MS (Mississippi News Now) - 50-year-old William Gilbert was denied bond in court on Wednesday.

He has been charged with two counts of culpable negligent homicide in addition to the charge of felony leaving the scene of an accident.

Two teenagers lost their lives in the hit-and-run accident that happened on Friday night. 15-year-old Promise Hampton and 13-year-old Bryan Jones were hit and killed by a Jeep Cherokee on Northside Drive near Del Rosa Street.

"She was a happy go lucky child, fun to be around. Always a jokester," said Phyllis Thomas, Promise's great aunt. "She loved to fish with her granddaddy. She loved family."

Jackson Police say initially Gilbert left the scene, but later turned himself in to Jackson Police.

A judge arraigned him Monday and the families are not pleased with the felony leaving the scene charge against him or the bond amount.

"This man got a $25,000 bond for killing two children and it was witnessed, by the people at that restaurant and people at the houses," added Thomas. "I want justice for my family, I want justice for Promise, a sweet spirit, and you wonder who could be so mean, why didn't you stop?"

"This case is still under investigation," said Jackson Police Commander Tyree Jones. "We do look forward to more charges once we have concluded our investigation and we deem it necessary to pursue more charges, but at this point that's where we are."

"OK, if it's felony fleeing what was he fleeing from?" asked Thomas. "What were those two bodies on the ground?  A 13 and 15-year-old bag of trash. That's my question to him and the whole law enforcement."

A vigil is set for both victims Thursday at 7 p.m. near the scene where this accident happened.

Funeral arrangements for both victims are pending.

This investigation is ongoing.

Vigil held for hit and run victims

JACKSON, MS (Mississippi News Now) - Strong emotions filled a candlelight vigil for two teens killed last week in a hit and run accident.

Promise Hampton and Bryan Jones were walking on Northside Drive and Del Rosa when they were struck by a Jeep Cherokee last Friday night. Their families, friends, members of Friends of Fallen Riders and the Hinds County Sheriff's Department gathered to remember the lives of the two teens.

"Cheerful, she always told jokes and everything," said Angel Adams, Promise's older sister. "We spent so much time together and I'm sad because I couldn't spend those last moments with her."

"Nobody likes to see a young life taken tragically like this. It's sickening," said Hinds County Sheriff Victor Mason. "People need to be cautious that children are playing. It's sad. These children were on the sidewalk so you can't drink and drive if that was the story, so they just need to be mindful and follow the rules of the road."

Hampton's grandfather, James Hampton, says Promise holds a special place in his heart. The two loved fishing together.

"I had just taken her fishing the week before she was killed but you know I'm going to miss my fishing buddy because she wasn't only my fishing buddy," said Hampton. "She was my heart, and she was my grandchild and I did really love her."

Jackson police upgraded charges for the man accused of hitting and killing both teens to culpable negligent homicide this week.  Although someone is being charged for the crime, both families say it doesn't replace the heartache of losing their loved ones.

"We all knew him for almost 20 years. He watch my granddaughter grow up. I don't have hard feelings for the man but what he did was wrong," said Hampton.

Both teens will be laid to rest this weekend.

Copyright 2016 MSNewsNow. All rights reserved.
